_about: Single source of truth for screening and triage rules. Every value has a source. PLACEHOLDER = no evidence yet; tune from team tests (Phase 6) and record the evidence here. Levels are in dB re: team baseline, never dB HL.

ears.source: Design choice: both ears, left first.

frequencies_hz.source: American Academy of Audiology (2011), Childhood Hearing Screening Guidelines, Summary of recommendations, pure tone screening, item 3: pure tone sweep at 1000, 2000 and 4000 Hz (at 20 dB HL). 500 Hz is controlled separately by policy_500hz.

screening_level_db_re_team_baseline.source: ASSUMPTION (owner decisions 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20): 20, mirroring the 20 dB HL school screening level of American Academy of Audiology (2011), Childhood Hearing Screening Guidelines, Summary of recommendations, pure tone screening item 3. Assumes the team baseline (calibration.baseline_dbfs: 7 adults, one phone+earphone pair, provisional) approximates audiometric zero; it is not an ISO reference, so levels are dB re: team baseline, never dB HL. At 1-4 kHz the baseline is an upper bound, so the tone may be more than 20 dB above the adults' real threshold.

ramp_ms.source: PLACEHOLDER. TODO(source): rise/fall time from a pure-tone audiometry standard. Purpose: avoid onset/offset clicks (ERR-005).

sample_rate_hz.source: Design choice: standard audio rate, same as the original app's tones.

peak_dbfs.source: Design choice: just below full scale to avoid clipping. Loudness is then set by the player volume and calibration.

uncalibrated_player_volume.source: PLACEHOLDER for Phase 4 device trials only: the spike's worn-earphone volume (docs/SPIKE.md §5). Used while screening_level_db_re_team_baseline is null; every such session is marked UNCALIBRATED.

min_response_ms.source: PLACEHOLDER: taps faster than this after tone onset are treated as anticipation, not hearing.

response_window_ms.source: PLACEHOLDER: a tap must come within this time after tone onset to count.

inter_stimulus_interval_ms.source: PLACEHOLDER: random gap range between presentations, so the child can't predict the rhythm.

timing_origin.source: Design choice (ERR-026): where response time and the response window start. play_call = when the app calls play(); playback_start = when the player reports playing. Both are logged per trial. Switched to playback_start on 2026-10-19 by the owner: B-3 play latency 144 / 486 / 2243 ms (CLAIMS P5-01) is variable, so play_call mis-times taps; taps from the reported start were 806-1481 ms (P5-02). Catch trials play a silent clip through the same path, so they use the same reference. Allowed: play_call | playback_start.

max_play_latency_ms.source: PLACEHOLDER (ERR-026): a presentation (tone or silent catch clip) whose reported playback start comes more than this after play(), or never, is invalid and replayed like a noise-gated tone (shares noise.max_replays_per_tone; then the point is 'not tested'). 1000 ms = tone.duration_ms: a start delayed by more than the whole stimulus is a pipeline stall, not normal output latency; it caps the silent wait in which a tap counts as an early response at under half the response window. On B-3 (no preloading) 13/16 starts were <= 832 ms and 3 were above (1078, 1208, 2243 ms, the last the first tone of the session). Re-measure with preloading in team tests.

presentations_per_point.source: PLACEHOLDER: tone presentations per ear and frequency per round.

min_hits_per_point.source: PLACEHOLDER: valid in-window responses needed to count a point as heard.

catch_trials.source: PLACEHOLDER: silent trials inserted at random per session.

min_catch_trials.source: PLACEHOLDER: below this, reliability can't be judged, so the outcome is RETEST.

max_false_alarm_rate.source: PLACEHOLDER: share of silent trials that got a tap. Above this, RETEST.

max_out_of_window_rate.source: PLACEHOLDER: share of tone trials with a tap outside the response window. Above this, RETEST.

gating_strategy.source: docs/SPIKE.md §5: metering keeps running during playback (spike step 7) and worn-earphone tone leakage at vol 0.10 stays within the room's own drift (scripts/analyze_spike.py). Allowed: during_tone | between_tones.

reference_quiet_db.source: PLACEHOLDER: quiet-room median metering on the spike phone (Redmi 2201117TI, scripts/analyze_spike.py, quiet-baseline clip, docs/SPIKE.md §5.3). Device-specific; re-measure per standard device in Phase 6. Relative mic level, not dB SPL.

ambient_measure_ms.source: PLACEHOLDER: length of the pre-test room-noise measurement (after mic settle).

gate_db_above_baseline.source: PLACEHOLDER. Gate = reference_quiet_db + this. Spike (scripts/analyze_spike.py, CLAIMS SPK-03/SPK-04): tone-on medians sit within a few dB of the quiet baseline; quiet vs corridor medians differ by more than 10. Tune from Phase 6 team tests.

max_replays_per_tone.source: PLACEHOLDER: a tone masked by noise is discarded and replayed at most this many times; then the point is 'too noisy'.

meter_poll_ms.source: Design choice: same poll rate as the spike, so a 1000 ms tone gets about 10 samples.

mic_settle_ms.source: Spike (CLAIMS SPK-01): first sample after mic start was -160 in 13/13 clips, then a start-up hump at ~0.4-0.63 s, settled by ~750 ms. 1000 ms adds margin.

invalid_at_or_below_db.source: Spike (CLAIMS SPK-01): -160 is a no-data floor (first sample, plug events); the lowest real sample in a quiet room was about -40. Samples at or below this are invalid, never 'quiet'.

saturated_at_or_above_db.source: Spike (CLAIMS SPK-02): metering tops out at about -1.0 (corridor noise, plug clicks). Saturated samples count as too loud.

plug_guard_ms.source: PLACEHOLDER: spike step 12 saw -1.0 spikes and -160 dropouts around plug/unplug, duration not measured. Samples within this window of any audio-device change are discarded (the test is paused anyway).

min_valid_samples_per_tone.source: PLACEHOLDER: fewer valid samples than this during a tone means noise is unknown, so the tone is replayed.

baseline_dbfs.source: 7 consenting adult volunteers, Redmi 2201117TI + Samsung wired earphones, media volume 6 steps, run 1, 2026-10-19; provisional. Measured run-1 medians of V1-V7, unmodified (scripts/calibrate.py; docs/CLAIMS.md CAL-01..03), both ears pooled, in dB re the tone file's full scale at player volume 1.0. 500 Hz is a measured median. 1000/2000/4000 Hz are UPPER BOUNDS limited by the phone's playback floor (docs/ERROR_LOG.md ERR-044), not true thresholds, so tones there may play louder than intended. A team baseline, not an ISO audiometric zero: levels are dB re: team baseline, never dB HL. null = not calibrated (tone.uncalibrated_player_volume, sessions marked UNCALIBRATED).

provisional.source: Owner decision 2026-10-20 (ERR-044): the baseline is provisional until the Stage 2 recalibration with a quieter 1-4 kHz tone set. While true (and calibrated), the result screen shows the result.provisional note.

device.source: Owner: standard device for Phase 6 (CLAUDE.md calibration context). Baseline values apply to this pair only.

media_volume_steps.source: docs/TEAM_TEST_PROTOCOL.md step 1 (loudness safety), owner, 2026-10-19: media volume at zero then up 6 steps; the loudest calibration level was comfortable. Redmi 2201117TI + Samsung wired earphones only. Every later session must use the same setting.

start_db.source: PLACEHOLDER: first presentation level of the threshold search, dB re full scale (player volume 0.01; the spike's comfortable worn level was 0.10 = -20 dB, docs/SPIKE.md).

step_down_db.source: PLACEHOLDER: 'down 10, up 5' bracketing, the usual manual pure-tone threshold method. TODO(source): cite a threshold-audiometry guideline.

heard_needed.source: PLACEHOLDER: threshold = lowest level heard on this many ascending presentations. TODO(source) with step_down_db.

min_db.source: Design choice: floor of the search (player volume ~0.00003). A threshold at the floor is reported as 'at floor', not as a value.

max_db.source: Design choice: player volume 1.0, the loudest the app can play at the fixed media volume.

outlier_db_above_group.source: PLACEHOLDER (owner request 2026-10-19): a run-1 threshold more than this above the median of the OTHER volunteers at that frequency counts as clearly higher. Three 5 dB steps: beyond the usual 5-10 dB test-retest spread of threshold measurement, TODO(source).

outlier_min_points.source: PLACEHOLDER: a volunteer with at least this many clearly-higher thresholds (of 8 ear x frequency points) is excluded from the baseline, so one stray answer doesn't exclude anyone.

max_presentations.source: PLACEHOLDER: per ear and frequency; then the search stops without a threshold.

player_volume.source: PLACEHOLDER: Telugu voice instructions through the earphones at the fixed media volume. Set by ear with real recordings (comfortable, not loud). Not a test level.

trials.source: PLACEHOLDER: left/right check presentations (random side), all must be answered correctly. Idea ported from the original DhwaniSarathi EarTest screen (Apache-2.0, ATTRIBUTION.md).

mode.source: Design choice: low tones are easily masked by room noise, so 500 Hz is only tested in a quiet room. Allowed: always | never | only_if_ambient_below.

ambient_threshold_db_re_baseline.source: PLACEHOLDER: ambient level above noise.reference_quiet_db at which 500 Hz is skipped.

enabled.source: Design choice: two-stage screening, matching American Academy of Audiology (2011), Childhood Hearing Screening Guidelines, Summary of recommendations, pure tone screening, item 7: rescreen immediately. Rescreen before any REFER.

failed_points_only.source: Design choice: only the ear/frequency points that were not heard.

max_rounds.source: Design choice: at most one rescreen round in the same session.

catch_trials.source: PLACEHOLDER: silent trials inserted into the rescreen round, so it can't be passed by tapping in rhythm.

value.en: Is there fluid or discharge from the ear?
value.te: చెవి నుండి నీరు, చీము లేదా ఏదైనా ద్రవం కారుతోందా?

value.en: Does the child have ear pain?
Has the child had a cold or blocked nose recently?
value.te: విద్యార్థికి ఇటీవల జలుబు గానీ ముక్కు దిబ్బడ గానీ ఉండిందా?

questions.source: TODO(source): checklist wording needs review by a clinician (CLAUDE.md: ask about medical wording). Telugu reviewed and approved by a native speaker (docs/TELUGU_REVIEW.md).

value.reason: Likely treatable cause reported (for example wax or infection): PHC first. Triage, not diagnosis.

rules.source: TODO(source): routing rule needs a citation and clinician review. First matching rule wins.

default_route.source: Design choice: no likely treatable cause reported, so route to the District Early Intervention Centre for further hearing assessment.

default_reason.value: No likely treatable cause reported: DEIC for further hearing assessment. Triage, not diagnosis.

value.en: Reminder: {child} ({school}) missed the ear-check camp{date}. Please contact the class teacher to book a new date. This is a screening follow-up, not a diagnosis.
value.te: రిమైండర్: {child} ({school}) {date} చెవి పరీక్ష క్యాంప్‌కు హాజరు కాలేదు. కొత్త తేదీ కోసం దయచేసి తరగతి ఉపాధ్యాయులను సంప్రదించండి. ఇది స్క్రీనింగ్ ఫాలో-అప్ మాత్రమే, వ్యాధి నిర్ధారణ కాదు.

missed_camp.source: Design choice: stubbed reminder (logged as 'would send', never sent; real SMS is a future cost). {date} is filled from "date" (en ' on 24 Oct 2026', te '24-10-2026 న', where Telugu puts the date before the camp) or empty when no camp is booked. Telugu reviewed and approved by a native speaker (docs/TELUGU_REVIEW.md #167).

frequencies_hz.source: DhwaniSarathi audiometer/app/utils/CONFIG.js FREQUENCY_PTS (250-8000 Hz), limited to the frequencies that have a team calibration baseline (calibration.baseline_dbfs) and a generated tone file (scripts/make_tones.py). 250 and 8000 Hz have neither. Same four frequencies as the WHO pure-tone average (hearing_grades).

levels_db_re_team_baseline.source: DhwaniSarathi audiometer/app/utils/CONFIG.js AMPLITUDE_PTS: ascending 10 dB steps from 0, first 'Yes' = threshold (their utils/Audiometry.js; they went up to 140). Levels are dB re: team baseline, played at calibration.baseline_dbfs + level. Each frequency stops at the loudest level the phone can play (baseline + level <= 0 dB re full scale): 30 at 500 Hz and 60 at 1-4 kHz with the provisional baseline. A tone not heard up to there is recorded as no response.

masking.source: Decision 2026-10-20 (owner asked to either use a proper noise file or drop the masked phase): dropped. The original's masked tone files carry near-silent noise (Day 1 audit), and we have no calibrated masking noise level, so a 'masked' phase would not be real masking. The original's results only used the unmasked thresholds.

hearing_grades.source: World Health Organization, World report on hearing (2021), Table 1, grades of hearing loss by pure-tone average of 500, 1000, 2000 and 4000 Hz: <20, 20-<35, 35-<50, 50-<65, 65-<80, 80-<95 and >=95 dB HL (Profound and Complete merged here as 80+, as in the original DhwaniSarathi Results.js). Grades proposed in Olusanya BO, Davis AC, Hoffman HJ (2019), Hearing loss grades and the International classification of functioning, disability and health, Bull World Health Organ 97(10):725-728, doi:10.2471/BLT.19.230367 (the reference cited in the original Results.js). WHO grades are in dB HL; the detailed test measures dB re: team baseline, so every grade it shows is an estimate and is labelled so.
